intro: An ordinary inverse requires a square nonsingular matrix. A pseudoinverse keeps only supported singular directions and also handles rectangular systems.
task: Compute a Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse using an explicit relative cutoff on singular values.
requirements: matrix is a nonempty real matrix. rcond is a scalar in [0,1].
Retain singular values strictly greater than rcond times the largest singular value. Replace other inverse singular values by zero.
Return an array with transposed shape. A zero matrix has a zero pseudoinverse; do not divide by zero when all singular values vanish.
Raise ValueError if the requested inverse or solution exceeds finite floating-point range, even when individual inputs satisfy the bounds.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Use a thin singular-value decomposition so the formula works for both tall and wide matrices.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Build a zero reciprocal vector first and fill only retained entries; preserve the strict cutoff comparison.

explanation: The pseudoinverse reverses each retained singular direction and leaves discarded directions at zero. Multiplying it by a target gives the minimum-norm least-squares solution under that cutoff.
The cutoff is relative to the largest singular value, so multiplying a matrix by a common nonzero scale preserves which directions survive. Equality with the threshold is deliberately discarded.
